scenarioStory.history: Husband states his wife has not been herself since this morning. He last saw her acting normally around 7:00 AM when she took her morning insulin injection. He found her slumped in a kitchen chair at approximately 9:45 AM, sweaty, and slurring her words when he tried to talk to her. She skipped breakfast because she got a phone call. An insulin pen and a used glucose test strip wrapper are on the kitchen table next to her.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 54-year-old female seated at the kitchen table, diaphoretic, with slurred speech and a slowed response to voice. Husband is present and provides history of insulin use and a skipped breakfast. → Oral glucose given: After 25 g of oral glucose, the patient's speech clears and she becomes oriented. Husband confirms this is consistent with prior low blood sugar episodes. → Transport initiated: Patient is packaged and transported, remaining alert and oriented with stable vital signs en route.

patientInformation.patientCondition: Altered mental status, husband reports "not acting right" since this morning

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find a 54-year-old female seated at the kitchen table, diaphoretic, with slurred speech and a slowed response to voice. Husband is present and provides history of insulin use and a skipped breakfast.
relatedChecklist: Primary survey; ensure airway remains patent, reposition as needed
Assess AVPU and Glasgow Coma Score
Perform validated stroke scale (facial droop, arm drift, speech)
Obtain SAMPLE history and last known well time from husband
Administer oral glucose gel 25 g PO (BGL 42 mg/dL, patient able to swallow)

scenarioEvents.name: Oral glucose given
scenarioEvents.description: After 25 g of oral glucose, the patient's speech clears and she becomes oriented. Husband confirms this is consistent with prior low blood sugar episodes.
relatedChecklist: Reassess vital signs and mental status after glucose administration
Transport to hospital; not all safe-release criteria are met

scenarioEvents.name: Transport initiated
scenarioEvents.description: Patient is packaged and transported, remaining alert and oriented with stable vital signs en route.
relatedChecklist: Continue reassessment of mental status and vitals en route to prevent complications

scenarioEvents.name: Oral glucose delayed
scenarioEvents.description: With glucose unchecked or oral glucose withheld, the patient's mental status continues to deteriorate. She is now unresponsive and unable to protect her own airway.
relatedChecklist: Recognize patient can no longer safely receive oral glucose
Position patient for airway protection; apply high-flow oxygen
Initiate immediate transport to closest appropriate receiving facility
